newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senate backs Clinton on Bosnia troop moves.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senate backs Clinton on Bosnia troop moves.

text.p: The U.S. Senate on Friday strongly urged but did not require the United States to pull out its troops from Bosnia by next June 30, giving the Clinton administration the flexibility it sought.
The House has voted to cut off funds for the troops on June 30, 1996, despite administration arguments that a mandatory date could threaten U.S. troops and jeapardize the mission.

The non-binding sense of the Senate amendment, offered by Michigan Democratic Sen. Carl Levin, passed on a voice vote on a bipartisan basis. It is part of a $268 billion defense spending bill which the Senate hoped to complete on Friday.
The Bosnia vote was a compromise that put the Senate on record as seeking an end to U.S. troop involvement within a year, but avoiding a confrontation with the administration.

Sen. Russell Feingold, a Wisconsin Democrat, initially sought a firmer cutoff date, saying without a deadline "the mission absolutely risks continuing for who knows how long." But he ended backing the Levin alternative.

The Levin measure stressed that the U.S. ground troops should complete the mission by June 30, 1998, and that Western European allies should be on notice they will have to provide a follow-up force as necessary.
